verdict.justification: Both deliverables are exceptionally well-constructed, accurately identifying the missing AP_TB-1.xlsx file, flagging all accounting exceptions (such as the Prepaid Insurance #1251 variance of $49,137.41, the Division 12 AR accrual of $60,500, and the post-close March adjustments), and adding the new April schedules at the end of the workbook. However, Deliverable A is superior in its accounting analysis of the Payroll Accrual (#2200) variance on Tab 14 and in its adherence to the prompt's exact file naming instructions on Tab 0. In Payroll-1.xlsx, the April accrual entries are -236,500 (130% accrual) and -20,500 (Special IT accrual), totaling 257,000, whereas the GL balance for #2200 is 141,033.00, resulting in a true schedule-to-GL difference of $115,967.00 (which equals the 198,300 March reversal minus the 257,000 April accruals vs the 118,767 period change in the GL). Deliverable A accurately calculates this $115,967 variance, whereas Deliverable B miscalculates the variance as $177,467.00. Additionally, Deliverable A explicitly references every single required source file by its exact name directly on the Table of Contents (Tab 0), whereas Deliverable B omits PPD1251-1.xlsx's duplicate cross-check and uses internal links ('#3a (links)') instead of exact file names in several rows on Tab 0.
